description: Finite, source-audited finding-ID registry and immutable/update-restriction catalogue for the Kubernetes manifest compatibility check. API rules are grounded in upstream Kubernetes validators, registry update strategies, and defaulting at the pinned commits. Repository-policy rules are project-defined graph/contract enforcement. This catalogue does not claim to be a universal Kubernetes immutability schema.

kubernetes.same_minor_extrapolation: A scenario declaring any other patch release inside a supported minor is reported with patch-coverage-extrapolated; the exact audited patches above anchor the minor's rule set. A scenario declaring any other minor fails configuration validation.

strategies.semantic-equal-immutable: Compare the field with API structural equality (apimachinery Semantic.DeepEqual semantics, including ordered arrays where upstream compares them) after applying the rule's recorded defaults; any difference is a violation.
strategies.whole-spec-immutable: The entire spec object is frozen; any change anywhere under spec is a violation.
strategies.baseline-gated-immutable: The field is frozen only when the baseline object sets the gate (for example ConfigMap/Secret immutable: true); the gate is read from the baseline, never the candidate.
strategies.conditional-immutable: The field is frozen only while a statically checkable condition holds on both revisions (for example both Service types are LoadBalancer).
strategies.transition-validated: The change is permitted only on specific source-verified transitions; all other transitions are violations.
strategies.allowlist-spec: Every spec field outside a named mutable allowlist is frozen; unfamiliar or newly added fields are violations by default.
strategies.completions-rule: Non-indexed Jobs freeze completions; Indexed Jobs may change completions only in tandem with an equal parallelism value.
strategies.job-template-rule: Job spec.template is frozen except for the suspended-Job exception family, whose eligibility depends on live status and feature gates that rendered YAML cannot prove.
strategies.pod-update-rule: Direct-Pod normal-update restrictions: only source-listed mutations are allowed; toleration matching ignores tolerationSeconds so existing NoExecute tolerations may edit that field.
strategies.quantity-transition: Parse and compare quantities numerically; classify the change under the rule's transition table instead of a blanket verdict.
strategies.ignored-update: The registry update strategy silently restores the previous value; the requested change is ineffective, not an API rejection.
strategies.selector-consistency: Validate that each workload's selector matches its own pod template labels under Kubernetes label-selector semantics.
strategies.selector-target-graph: Evaluate unchanged consumer selectors against candidate target templates in the same namespace and report lost selection relationships.
strategies.reference-graph: Apply the required-reference transition table to locally resolvable consumer references.
strategies.label-drift: Report baseline label removals and value changes that no stronger rule already covers.
strategies.protected-contract: Enforce explicitly declared protected labels and protected resources regardless of visible consumers.
strategies.removal-policy: Report removed baseline objects; block only for protected identities or proven local dependency losses.
strategies.conditional-risk: Report a change whose safety cannot be decided from rendered YAML alone because it depends on live state or feature gates; never assert an API rejection.
strategies.coverage-reporting: Report rule or patch coverage boundaries without implying a compatibility verdict.
strategies.exception-diagnostics: Report exception configuration that matched nothing on a requested baseline.

guards: Mutable allowlist in these minors: replicas, ordinals, template, updateStrategy, revisionHistoryLimit, persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy, minReadySeconds. Any other spec field, including newly introduced fields unknown to this check, is forbidden.
rules.coverage_note: Applies only to Kubernetes 1.35 and 1.36, whose validators freeze the whole spec outside the mutable allowlist. The 1.37 validator checks the four named immutable fields directly, so this rule is inactive there; a spec field outside both sets is unrestricted in 1.37 and unknown-field changes there are reported as rule-coverage-partial.

guards: revision is mutable despite the function comment claiming otherwise; only data is frozen.

Only an explicitly authored selector is compared. A selector present on exactly one side is handled as a conditional case (the API server generates selectors on create); never fabricate the missing side, and report unresolved one-sided differences under conditional-update-risk.
An omitted value defaults to NonIndexed; compare after defaulting.

Default completions and parallelism to 1 only under the source's actual conditions (both omitted). Non-indexed Jobs freeze completions entirely. Indexed Jobs may set completions to a new value only when it equals the candidate parallelism; Indexed Jobs cannot set completions to nil.

Container image and command changes are definite violations. Scheduling directives, labels, annotations, schedulingGates, and suspended-Job container resource changes have version-, gate-, and status-dependent exceptions: eligibility requires live Job status (suspended and never started) plus feature gates that rendered YAML cannot prove, so unresolved cases are reported under conditional-update-risk. Missing status in YAML is never evidence of never-started state.

rules.coverage_note: spec.scheduling is new in 1.37 and carries feature-gated declarative update restrictions (validateJobSchedulingUpdate). This check inventories the field and reports changes as partial coverage; it does not certify or reject them. Not present in 1.35/1.36 rule sets.

guards: Allowed updates for a direct Pod object: container and initContainer image changes; activeDeadlineSeconds may only be set or decreased; tolerations may be added, and an existing toleration's tolerationSeconds may be edited (the validator's old-entry matching ignores tolerationSeconds in all three audited versions); schedulingGates may only be removed; gated scheduling-directive exceptions apply. Removal or key/operator/value/effect mutation of an existing toleration without preserving the original entry is forbidden. Resource-resize and ephemeral-container subresources are not normal Helm/Kustomize update paths. This rule applies only to direct Pod objects, never to a workload pod template.

rules.coverage_note: Known-mutable rule: CronJob jobTemplate changes affect future Jobs only and have no update-time immutability restriction in the audited sources. Recorded so the check does not apply Job-template immutability to CronJob. Emits no findings on its own.

guards: The gate is the baseline object's immutable: true, never the candidate's. When gated: unsetting the flag and changing effective data or binaryData are violations. Changing data while first setting immutable (baseline gate unset) is allowed. Metadata changes are not data changes.

The gate is the baseline object's immutable: true, never the candidate's. When gated: unsetting the flag and changing effective data (stringData applied over decoded data) are violations. Changing data while first setting immutable (baseline gate unset) is allowed.
An omitted type defaults to Opaque; compare after defaulting. Unconditional: independent of the immutable flag.

rules.coverage_note: resource.k8s.io/v1 is the served stable API in all three audited minors; the v1beta2 form is a separate API and is inventory only.

guards: Other ResourceSlice fields are not blanket-frozen.
API-populated caller identity fields in spec are ignored. The finding describes an ignored, ineffective update, never an API rejection.

rules.coverage_note: certificates.k8s.io/v1 ClusterTrustBundle exists only in the audited 1.37 source. In 1.35/1.36 the kind is served only as v1beta1/v1alpha1, which are inventory-only in this delivery: beta ClusterTrustBundle objects are reported as rule-coverage-partial, never silently compared under this stable rule.

certificates.k8s.io/v1 PodCertificateRequest exists only in the audited 1.37 source. In 1.35/1.36 the kind is served only as v1beta1, which is inventory-only: beta objects are reported as rule-coverage-partial.

guards: One-time initialization exception: spec.csi.controllerExpandSecretRef may go from unset to set; that specific transition is not a violation. The persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy is mutable and deliberately not covered by any rule.
An omitted value defaults to Filesystem; compare after defaulting.

rules.coverage_note: nodeAffinity is immutable only when the MutablePVNodeAffinity feature gate is disabled and only once already set; the gate state is live cluster state that rendered YAML cannot resolve. Changes are reported as conditional risk, never as a definite rejection.
Mutability depends on the VolumeAttributesClass feature gate and, once set, on live status.currentVolumeAttributesClassName; neither is provable from rendered YAML. Reported as conditional risk.

guards: An omitted value defaults to Filesystem; compare after defaulting. Unconditional; no exceptions.
One-time initialization: unset to set is allowed exactly once; any other change is a violation.

Two narrow migrations are allowed: beta annotation volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class to an equal field value, and unset-to-set when no conflicting old annotation exists. All other changes are violations.

Quantities compare numerically. A decrease is not universally rejected: with failed-expansion recovery enabled (or after any prior expansion attempt) a bounded reduction above live capacity is accepted, and live capacity is unknowable from YAML. An increase is never blocked by update validation, but whether it provisions depends on StorageClass allowVolumeExpansion and CSI driver support. Both directions are conditional risks; neither is certified nor rejected.
rules.coverage_note: Requires the RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure feature-gate state and live status.capacity for decreases, and StorageClass/driver capability for increases; none are provable offline.

Free while status.currentVolumeAttributesClassName is unset, frozen once set; both the gate and the live status are unknowable from rendered YAML. Reported as conditional risk, not a global immutable rule.

guards: Only explicitly declared addresses are compared; an absent server allocation is never treated as a removal. The primary address (index 0) must not change once set. Releasing a secondary address requires ipFamilyPolicy SingleStack in the same update. Transitions involving ExternalName or headless services are exempt from this check. type, selector, and nodePort are not generally immutable.
Headless-state transitions are exempt. The primary family must not change; validated secondary-family add/remove transitions are permitted.
Applies only while both baseline and candidate Service types are LoadBalancer; a type change away from LoadBalancer resets the constraint.
Applies only while both baseline and candidate are LoadBalancer services with externalTrafficPolicy Local; outside that condition the field is free to change.

rules.rationale: A workload whose selector does not match its own pod template cannot roll out; this is logical invalidity of the rendered declaration itself, checked for candidate resources whether or not any baseline exists. Emits render-validation findings that are never waivable.
guards: Selector semantics follow Kubernetes matchLabels/matchExpressions with missing-key semantics for In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist. Empty and nil selector meanings are API-specific, not one generic default.

rules.rationale: An unchanged consumer selector that matched a baseline target template and no longer matches its candidate template is a proven local discovery regression. First graph consumers: same-namespace Service selectors (absent or empty selects nothing), policy/v1 PodDisruptionBudget selectors (nil selects none, empty selects all), and NetworkPolicy top-level podSelector (empty selects all local targets). Relational finding: consumer is the primary resource, target is the related resource; one finding per baseline consumer/target pair.
guards: Only unchanged consumer selectors can prove a regression; a changed consumer selector is reported by mutable-selector-changed instead. Value edits, label removal, added labels affecting negative expressions, and target disappearance all count. The finding reports a lost declared selection relationship, never an asserted outage or running Pod count.

rules.rationale: A changed consumer selector is legal at the API level but silently re-targets traffic, disruption budgeting, or policy application; the candidate set of matched targets cannot certify unseen external consumers. Warn, never error.

A required reference whose baseline target, key, or port resolved locally and no longer does is a proven local dependency regression. In candidate validation context (reference resolves to a declared local object but the requested key or port is missing) the same ID is a non-waivable render-validation finding. Supported reference scope: container and initContainer env valueFrom key refs, envFrom refs, volumes and projected ConfigMap/Secret sources and items, ServiceAccount name, RoleBinding roleRef, Ingress Service/port backends, and Service named targetPort.
guards: Consumer slots match by container/env/volume/reference names, not list positions. Transition table applies: ended reliance (removed slot or reference replaced by non-reference data) produces no finding; candidate optionality suppresses absence findings; retargeting to a locally resolving target is compatible; retargeting to an unresolved target is external-reference-unverified. Optional unresolved references never produce dependency findings.

rules.rationale: A reference that is new or already external and remains unresolved cannot prove cluster absence; it may be supplied by another bundle. Warn, never error, and never misclassify a formerly local loss as this case.
A baseline metadata or pod-template label removed with no stronger evidence may break unknown external consumers that discover objects by label; unproven external reliance warns rather than blocks.
guards: Label additions alone never produce this finding; they warn only via a supported graph or contract regression. Protected labels are handled by protected-label-changed.

rules.rationale: A baseline label value change has the same unproven external-consumer risk as a removal, and also affects negative selector expressions; it warns rather than blocks.
guards: Protected labels are handled by protected-label-changed.

rules.rationale: An explicitly declared protected label that lost its baseline key or changed its baseline value violates a declared contract, independent of any consumer visible in the render. Evidence is the declaration itself, so this blocks in enforce mode.
guards: Protected label entries declare a JSON Pointer location and nonempty keys; baseline key/value pairs are preserved, not a universal fixed label set.

rules.rationale: A removed baseline object may break external clients, but rotating generated ConfigMap/Secret names is normal; blocking requires a proven local dependency or an explicit protected contract. Unprotected removals stay visible as warnings. No name-hash heuristics or automatic pairing of renamed objects.
guards: Generated-resource rotation is not inferred from hash-looking names; each revision resolves its own generated references, and successfully retargeted references are not losses.

rules.rationale: Removing an explicitly protected resource identity violates a declared contract and blocks in enforce mode regardless of visible consumers.

Shared reporting ID for changes whose safety depends on live state, feature gates, or unspecified defaults that rendered YAML cannot resolve. The finding names exactly what cannot be known offline; it never asserts an API rejection or a certified success.

Unsupported kinds, fields, or API versions and skipped object classes (Helm hooks, CRDs, custom resources) produce visible partial-coverage records so a clean report never silently certifies unchecked content.
A scenario declaring a patch release other than the exact audited patch of its minor receives rule coverage extrapolated from the audited source; the report must say so explicitly.
An exception configured for a requested baseline that matched no finding is stale configuration drift and must stay visible; exceptions for unrequested baselines are unused provenance, not stale.
